verdict.rationale: ClickHouse's official clickhousectl CLI can create and manage ClickHouse Cloud clusters and resources, and launch local servers. Cloud pricing scales idle services to zero, which partly supports the 'cheap' angle. Nothing shows this works as a per-agent or per-tenant fleet at the scale of thousands. Missing for 10: evidence of creating thousands of isolated databases cheaply, per-tenant/preview/branching provisioning patterns, a documented fleet-management API, and independent or hands-on corroboration of fleet-scale provisioning.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can cheaply create thousands of isolated databases — one per agent, tenant, or preview — and manage the fleet programmatically

citations.quote: Set up ClickHouse Cloud and create cloud-managed ClickHouse clusters * Create and manage ClickHouse Cloud Postgres services * Manage ClickHouse Cloud resources
With clickhousectl you can: * Install and manage local ClickHouse versions * Launch and manage local ClickHouse servers
pay only for the compute and storage you use, scaled separately and down to zero when idle
